answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents form clustered networks where an open meadow of worker nodes routes claims through a dense grove of randomized auditors. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditing enforces stake slashing on collateralized bonds if cross-audits detect collusion. Concurrently, topological cut verifications across transaction paths act like a defensive river, restricting sparse bottlenecks and imposing superlinear attacker cost.
